rapport_notes: Stayed calm and solution-oriented when the customer vented about being transferred to four different people, and gave him a concrete personal fix.
process_discipline_notes: No differentiator was repeated (none were said); no open-ended rubric question was asked so no silence to lose.

evidence_quotes.agenda: not asked — this is a follow-up call after an earlier virtual walkthrough, revisiting a previously-sent quote
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: "it's just gonna come down to, you know, if it's $2,000 difference. That's huge." / Jules: "Awesome. Of course." — a real price-comparison concern was raised and got no follow-up question about what it's being compared against.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: "You only actually pay with the hours used... if it took us less time to pack everything or less time to move everything, that is the only amount you're gonna pay for." — covers pay-less-if-faster; the other four Save Your Ass lines are not covered.

top_strength: Gave a precise, personalized two-day packing-and-moving estimate (crew size, hours, and dollar range for both weekday and weekend options) tied directly to specifics from the earlier walkthrough.
coaching_note: Customer explicitly flagged that a $2,000 gap vs. a competing quote would be the deciding factor and got no follow-up question — that's exactly the kind of concern that needs a second layer ('what's the other quote include?') instead of a pivot to 'I'll send the email.'
